setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and a neutral spine.
Extend both arms straight out to the sides or down at your sides with elbows soft but extended.
steps: Initiate a smooth circular motion with both arms moving in a forward direction.
Trace controlled circles through a full, pain-free range of motion, passing through flexion, adduction, and extension.
Maintain a steady, rhythmic pace while keeping the torso still and core engaged.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically throughout the movement without holding your breath.
cues: Keep ribs down and core brace engaged.
Move from the shoulders, not the torso.

common_faults.fault: Excessive arching of the lower back as the arms pass overhead.
common_faults.correction: Brace the abdominals and keep the ribs tucked to maintain a neutral spine.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders excessively up toward the ears.
common_faults.correction: Allow natural scapular movement without forcing a sustained shrug.

common_faults.fault: Bending the elbows to compensate for limited shoulder mobility.
common_faults.correction: Keep the arms long and reduce the circle diameter if full range causes elbow flexion.

precautions: If you feel shoulder impingement or sharp pain, decrease the size of the circles or stop the movement.

name: Forward Arm Circle
summary: A dynamic shoulder mobility exercise where the arms perform continuous circular rotations forward to warm up the shoulder girdle.
